Below From Mika in Joi's office: 
the procedure for the tourist visa is almost the same as the business visa. 
The difference is that a Japanese travel agency needs to be a host and issue all 
those letters and trip schedule, instead of a Japanese company for a business 
visa. 
If you can hire a Japanese travel agency somehow for booking their travels, that 
can be an option. 
But since we don't know any agency in Japan, we can't help for tourist visa. 
There's no simple tourist visa for Russians in Japan, unfortunately. 
Best regards, 
Mika

Embassy or a Consulate-General of Japan in the cities 
nearby.

companies, such as you are an employee of the subsidiary 
or something like that.

Subject Which Hyatt in Tokyo? 
There are 2 Hyatt's in Tokyo: 
Grand Hyatt Tokyo 
http://tokyo.grand.hyatt.com/en/hoteliour-hotel.html 
The Grand Hyatt is located in the "Roppongi Area" which is considered the Financial District. It 
is a 5 star hotel and you would receive all of the Centurian Amenities. 
Park Hyatt Tokyo 
http://www.tokyo.park.hyatt.com/en/hotel/our-hotel.html 
The Park Hyatt is located in the "Shinjuku Area" which is considered the museum/theater area. It 
is a 5 Star hotel but you would not receive all of the Centurian Amenities here.. 
I am told the two hotels are not that far from each other. 
Which hotel do you prefer? Grand or Park?
